newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Multiple faults found in Israel bridge disaster.
newsitem.headline: Multiple faults found in Israel bridge disaster.

text.p: An Israeli inquiry into the collapse of a pedestrian bridge that killed two Australians at the start of the "Jewish Olympics" found on Wednesday that faulty design, materials and construction led to the disaster.

The seven-member committee, chaired by the former chief engineer of the Israeli army, submitted its findings to the government, but refrained from recommending any criminal indictments pending completion of a police investigation.

Competitors from the 370-member Australian team to the 51-nation Maccabiah Games were walking across the bridge over the Yarkon River on July 14 when it buckled as they prepared to enter a stadium near Tel Aviv for the opening of the games.
Two Australians from Sydney -- ten-pin bowler Greg Small, 37, and 50-year-old Yetty Bennet, section manager of the men's bowling team -- were killed and 43 delegation members were injured.
The committee chairman, retired brigadier Ishai Dotan, read from a list of faults which the inquiry pinned on the engineer who designed the wood and metal bridge and the contractors who built it.

"Faulty coordination between those who carried out the work and the (bridge's) designer. Complete absence of a system of supervision and control. Work performed without blueprints and instructions. Use of low-grade materials and reliance on elements taken from stock," he told a news conference.
The committee found the bridge had not been designed to the stress specifications which the engineer said he had set.
"The design was extremely faulty and wrong from the start," it said.
Police have already questioned the engineer, contractors and the organisers of the 15th Maccabiah competition. Israeli media reports said criminal charges were likely against some of them.
One of the two contractors who built the bridge contested the findings.
"The materials we used were completely new. We had them in stock but we had never used them before," contractor Yehoshu Ben-Ezra told reporters.

Asked about the findings, Edgar Small, the father of the dead Australian sportsman, told Israeli Army Radio: "This whole episode of the bridge, I feel is a failure of firstly the Maccabiah games organisers and the Israeli government as well."
He said in the interview from Australia that he had not received a single condolence telephone call or card from anyone in the Israeli government.
